promises.d: A 03:40 landing is a normal pickup time here, not a problem to solve at the desk. The name is the opening hours, not a slogan.
Twenty cars, each one photographed and priced on its own page. You book that car, not a category with 'or similar' printed next to it.
Collect at arrivals, drop in town. Two locations, ten minutes apart, no fee for using both.
Nineteen of the twenty cars are automatic, which matters on Albanian mountain roads more than anywhere you have driven before.
One number, answered by someone in Tirana who can move a car. Not a queue, not a chatbot.

faq.q: How do I actually book a car?
faq.a: Send the dates, the car you want and your flight number by WhatsApp or phone. You get a written confirmation on WhatsApp. There is no checkout to fight with and no account to create.

faq.q: Is there a deposit?
faq.a: A deposit is settled at the desk when you collect, not through this website, and nothing is taken before then. The amount and whether it is cash or a card hold depend on the car, so ask when you send your dates and it comes back in writing with the total, before you travel.

faq.q: Do I pay online?
faq.a: No. Nothing is charged in advance and no card details are taken through this website. You settle at pickup, once you have seen the car.

faq.q: Is the price per day the final price?
faq.a: The rates on this site are the published daily rates, per car, in euro. Ask for the total for your exact dates before you commit and it comes back in writing, so there is nothing left to discover at the desk.

faq.q: Is it cheaper for a longer rental?
faq.a: Usually yes. The per-day rate drops as the rental gets longer, so a week is not simply seven times the daily price. Send the dates and ask for the total.

faq.q: Can I change or cancel?
faq.a: Plans move, especially with flights. Tell us as early as you can by WhatsApp and we will confirm the change in writing. Ask for the cancellation terms when you book so you have them from the start.

faq.q: Is the car in the photo the car I get?
faq.a: Yes. You book a named car, not a category with 'or similar' beside it. Every photograph on this site is the car itself, taken by the office. If you want a fresh one, ask and it comes back with the confirmation.

faq.q: Are the cars automatic?
faq.a: Nineteen of the twenty are automatic. The only manual is the Golf 5, which is also the cheapest car on the board at 30 euro a day. On Albanian mountain roads the automatic is worth having.

faq.q: Do you have a seven-seater?
faq.a: Two: both Hyundai Santa Fe, at 60 euro a day. They are the cars to take on the Lake Koman ferry or into the northern valleys with luggage.

faq.q: Which car should I take for the mountains?
faq.a: Something with ground clearance. The Tucson or a Santa Fe handle the track into Theth and the last stretch to the Blue Eye. A low sedan will manage the motorways and the coast road but not the rough final kilometres.

faq.q: Can I add a second driver or a child seat?
faq.a: Both are normal requests. Mention them in the same message as your dates and they are arranged before you arrive, with the cost confirmed in writing.

faq.q: What is my licence situation?
faq.a: An EU, UK or US licence is used routinely here. Licences printed in a non-Latin alphabet should be accompanied by an International Driving Permit, which you have to obtain in your own country before travelling, not on arrival. Bring the physical card.

faq.q: What are the roads actually like?
faq.a: Better than the reputation. The SH1 north to Shkodër and the SH2 are motorway standard. The coast road over the Llogara pass and the routes into the north are narrow, steep, spectacular and slower than any map will tell you. Add time rather than confidence.

faq.q: Can I take the car to Kosovo, Montenegro or Greece?
faq.a: Crossing a border needs a green card insurance document prepared in advance, so it has to be arranged when you book and never on the day. Ask before you plan the route.

faq.q: Is parking difficult in Tirana?
faq.a: Central Tirana is busy and paid parking around the Blloku district fills up. Most hotels have an arrangement. Outside the capital, parking is rarely a problem at all.

faq.q: Anything about driving here I should know?
faq.a: Drive on the right. Headlights are expected outside towns, seatbelts are required, and the alcohol limit is effectively zero if you have held a licence under ten years. Livestock on rural roads is normal and not a joke.

faq.q: Are you really open at 4am?
faq.a: Yes. Both offices are staffed around the clock, seven days, which is what the name is about. Night arrivals from Istanbul and Rome are ordinary here, not a special request.

faq.q: Where exactly do I meet you at the airport?
faq.a: Send your flight number with the booking and the meeting point comes back in your written confirmation, along with the name of the person who will be there.

faq.q: Can I collect at the airport and return in the city?
faq.a: Yes. The two offices are about ten minutes apart and using both is normal. Say which one you want for the return when you book.

faq.q: Can you deliver the car to my hotel?
faq.a: Inside Tirana this is a common arrangement. Ask when you book and it is confirmed in writing with any cost stated up front.

faq.q: How does fuel work?
faq.a: Confirm the fuel arrangement in your written confirmation so it is agreed before you drive away. The fuel stations nearest both offices are open through the night.

roads.name: The Albanian Riviera
roads.carWhy: The one drive that earns a roof you can drop.
roads.story: The road climbs to a thousand metres at Llogara, turns a corner, and the whole Ionian coast is suddenly below you. Then it drops through Dhërmi and Himarë to water that has no business being that colour. This is the drive people fly here for.

roads.name: North to the Accursed Mountains
roads.best: June to September, closed in winter
roads.carWhy: The last hour to Theth is not a sedan road.
roads.story: The SH1 runs fast and flat to Shkodër, then the country stands up. The final climb into Theth is a mountain pass with a valley of stone houses at the end of it. Ground clearance is not optional on this one.

roads.name: Berat and Gjirokastër
roads.carWhy: Long, smooth kilometres. Take the comfortable boot.
roads.story: Two Ottoman towns, both UNESCO listed, both built as stacked stone windows on a hillside. Easy roads the whole way, which makes this the trip to hand to someone who is nervous about driving abroad.

destinations.name: Ksamil
destinations.carWhy: Long motorway run, take the comfortable one.
destinations.note: Three small islands close enough to swim to, in water that looks edited. Go in June or September: in August the road in is a car park and the beaches are full by nine.

destinations.name: The Blue Eye
destinations.carWhy: The last stretch is a rough track.
destinations.note: A spring nobody has found the bottom of, pushing cold water up through a pupil of dark blue. Park at the gate and walk the last kilometre. Swimming is officially discouraged and the water is about ten degrees anyway.

destinations.name: Butrint
destinations.note: Greek, Roman, Venetian and Ottoman ruins stacked in a forest on a lagoon, and a UNESCO site since 1992. Two unhurried hours. Go early, before the tour buses arrive from Corfu.

destinations.name: Gjirokastër
destinations.carWhy: Hills all the way, and cobbles at the end.
destinations.note: The stone city, built in slate and shuttered windows up a steep hillside under an enormous castle. The old town streets are cobbled and severe: park below and climb.

destinations.name: Lake Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Seven seats, and it takes the ferry with you.
destinations.note: A working ferry through a flooded canyon that people compare to the fjords and Halong Bay, and for once the comparison holds. The car goes on the boat. Book the crossing ahead in summer.

destinations.name: Valbona valley
destinations.hours: 5 h, or via the Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Gravel and river crossings. Ground clearance matters.
destinations.note: Alpine valley at the top of the country, and the start of the Valbona to Theth walk if you have a spare day. Snowed in through winter, so June to September only.

destinations.name: Krujë
destinations.carWhy: Half a day out. Take the cheapest key on the board.
destinations.note: Skanderbeg's castle above an Ottoman bazaar of carpets and copper. The easiest real day trip from Tirana, and the one to do on your first afternoon while you get used to the roads.

destinations.name: Shkodër and Rozafa
destinations.carWhy: Fast, flat motorway the whole way.
destinations.note: A castle on a ridge where three rivers and a lake meet, and the best sunset view in northern Albania. The city below is flat, green and full of bicycles.

You get the total for your exact dates, where to meet us, and the name of the person who will be there. In writing, so nothing is left to discover at the desk.

Tirana airport arrivals or the city office on Rruga Njazi Meka, ten minutes apart. Both are staffed around the clock, so a 03:40 landing is an ordinary pickup here and not a special request. Give us the flight number and the car waits if you are late.

Basic insurance and unlimited kilometres inside Albania are in the daily rate. The motorways north and south are fast, the coast road over Llogara and the routes into the mountains are slower and better than any map suggests.
Return it to either office, whichever suits the end of your trip, at whatever hour your flight leaves. Tell us in advance if you want to swap which one and it costs nothing.
